title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-routing-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally hit sudden burst demand from priority tenants which caused noisy scaling behavior and poor utilization signals. This PR improves autoscaler priority-routing integration, adds burst token-bucket smoothing for priority queues, and surfaces per-priority utilization reporting in the fleet telemetry dashboards. Scope: - Add priority-aware routing hooks so requests tagged with priority_level are routed through token-bucket admission controls; ensure compatibility with existing fallback policies. - Implement burst smoothing (token-bucket with leaky refill) to avoid sharp autoscaler churn from short spikes. - Emit new telemetry: dedicated.fleet.utilization.per_priority, dedicated.autoscaler.burst_in_admit, and queueing.latency.p50/p95 per priority. - Add config knobs: autoscaler.priority_burst_window_ms, autoscaler.tokenbucket_refill_ms, and telemetry.priority_sampling_rate. Checklist: - [x] Design doc updated (Linear ENG-2145) - [x] Unit tests for token-bucket logic - [x] Integration test in perf-canary harness - [x] Docs & example configs added - [x] Telemetry dashboards updated Approach: Introduced a PriorityRouter abstraction to keep legacy routing unchanged for untagged requests. TokenBucket smoothing implemented in dedicated/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go with deterministic, testable time source. Telemetry uses existing metrics client with priority tag; added aggregation keys in observability-pack for dashboards. Rollout plan: Canary deploy autoscaler changes to fleet-us-west-2/dedicated-small, monitor dedicated.fleet.utilization.per_priority and autoscaler decision traces for 48h, then gradual rollout. Related: ENG-2273 (fleet SLO tuning), SUP-789 (customer incident with priority spike).
commits_summary: 1) add PriorityRouter + unit tests || 2) implement tokenbucket smoothing and deterministic clock || 3) emit per-priority telemetry metrics + aggregator keys || 4) add config schema and default values || 5) update dashboards and docs || 6) fix race in autoscaler reconcile observed in perf canary
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice clean abstraction for PriorityRouter. Left nits around naming and a question about fallback order for mixed-priority batches.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed naming nits and added explicit fallback tests for mixed-priority batches in reconcile_test.go.
Rita Singh: TokenBucket logic looks good, but we saw a race on canary when reconcile loop concurrently updated metrics. Recommend moving metric emission outside the reconcile lock.
Maya Chen (author): Moved emission to async snapshot path and added defensive nil checks; added comment linking to monitoring playbook.
Diego Alvarez: Can we expose the token bucket state via /debug endpoint for on-call debugging? If so please add a feature flag.
Maya Chen (author): Added debug exposure behind config flag autoscaler.debug_expose_tokenbucket=true and documented in runbook.
merge_details: Merged by Rita Singh on 2026-03-02 using squash merge. Commit message: 'dedicated: priority routing + tokenbucket burst smoothing + telemetry (ENG-2145, ENG-2273)'. Release notes: see field release_notes.
release_notes: Enhanced dedicated autoscaler: priority-aware routing, token-bucket burst smoothing to reduce scaling churn, and per-priority utilization metrics for better visibility. Configs: autoscaler.priority_burst_window_ms (default 5000), autoscaler.tokenbucket_refill_ms (default 100), telemetry.priority_sampling_rate (default 0.1). Rollout: canary then staged rollout.
notes_for_oncall: If customers report delayed handling of short bursts, check dedicated.autoscaler.burst_in_admit and tokenbucket refill rate. Use /debug/tokenbucket when autoscaler.debug_expose_tokenbucket=true. Monitor dedicated.fleet.utilization.per_priority for abnormal drops and queueing.latency.p95.
